gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.full: The store is full! Put a mana pool next to it, or add a Reservoir Upgrade.
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.redst: Redstone told us to rest. Check the lever!
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip0: Different kinds of flowers grow better together: that's harmony!
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip1: Fortune Upgrades make some cycles bloom with extra mana.
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip2: Bind the greenhouse to a mana pool with the Wand of the Forest, and I'll keep it filled.
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip3: Put a mana tablet in the blue slot and I'll charge it for you.
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip4: Growth Upgrades make the flowers grow faster. Zoom!
gui.alfheimheart.greenhouse.keeper.tip5: No fuel, no water, no fuss: just love and mana~
alfheimheart.lexicon.greenhouse0: The $(item)Mana Greenhouse$() is a little house of glass and livingwood in which up to eight $(thing)generating flowers$() grow with no fuel, no water and no care at all.$(br2)It gathers the mana they make in a store of its own and hands it on.
alfheimheart.lexicon.greenhouse1: Plant generating flowers in the eight beds round its mana heart. Every $(thing)cycle$() (five seconds) the flowers make mana, each as much as it would at its best, and together they grow better still: every kind of flower past the first adds 5 percent of $(thing)harmony$().
alfheimheart.lexicon.greenhouse2: The mana flows on into $(item)mana pools$(), $(item)spreaders$() and other receivers right next to it, or into one bound to it: touch the greenhouse with the $(l:botania:basics/wand)Wand of the Forest$(/l) in bind mode, then the receiver.
alfheimheart.lexicon.greenhouse3: The blue slot on the right charges $(item)mana tablets$(), mirrors and rings. The buttons in its window set how it heeds $(thing)redstone$() and whether it gives its mana away, and a $(item)comparator$() reads how full it is.$(br2)Its keeper will gladly tell you what it needs.
alfheimheart.lexicon.greenhouse4: The $(item)Heart of the Greenhouse$() is born on the $(l:botania:basics/terrasteel)Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate$(/l).
alfheimheart.lexicon.upgrades0: A greenhouse takes four $(item)upgrades$() in the slots on the left of its window. Upgrades of a kind stack, and up to eight of a kind count.$(br2)They are made from a $(item)Blank Floral Tablet$() on the $(l:botania:basics/rune_altar)Runic Altar$(/l).
alfheimheart.lexicon.upgrades2: $(item)Growth$(): each one makes the cycles a quarter faster.
alfheimheart.lexicon.upgrades3: $(item)Reservoir$(): each one makes room for 350 000 more mana.
alfheimheart.lexicon.upgrades4: $(item)Fortune$(): each one gives a cycle one more chance in ten to be lucky and bring half as much mana again.
alfheimheart.lexicon.upgrades5: $(item)Abundance$(): each one makes every cycle bring 15 percent more mana.
jei.alfheimheart.info.greenhouse: Grows up to eight generating flowers inside, with no fuel, water or care, and gathers their mana. Every cycle the flowers make as much mana as they would at their best; different kinds together grow better (harmony). The mana goes into mana pools, spreaders and other receivers next to it or bound to it with the Wand of the Forest, and charges the mana item in its blue slot.
jei.alfheimheart.info.heart: The living core of the Mana Greenhouse, made on the Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate.
jei.alfheimheart.info.upgrades: Mana Greenhouse upgrades, carved from a Blank Floral Tablet on the Runic Altar. Growth: faster cycles. Reservoir: more room for mana. Fortune: a chance for a cycle to bring extra mana. Abundance: more mana every cycle. Upgrades of a kind stack in its four upgrade slots.
block.alfheimheart.elven_portal.tip: A whole Alfheim gateway in one block: the elves trade what you put in, for mana
gui.alfheimheart.portal.portal.drop: Click the portal with an item to send it through
gui.alfheimheart.portal.status.idle: Waiting for something the elves take
gui.alfheimheart.portal.status.no_mana: Closed: not enough mana for a trade
gui.alfheimheart.portal.status.output_fu: Waiting: the output slots are full
gui.alfheimheart.portal.offered: The elves offer %s trades (JEI shows them under Elven Trade)
gui.alfheimheart.portal.pool: Draws mana from the mana pool beside it
gui.alfheimheart.portal.no_pool: Put a mana pool beside it, or aim a mana spreader at it
gui.alfheimheart.portal.redstone.high: Works only with a redstone signal
gui.alfheimheart.portal.redstone.low: Works only without a redstone signal
gui.alfheimheart.portal.slot.input.tip: Livingwood, manasteel, mana diamonds, mana pearls, mana glass, quartz, ores...
gui.alfheimheart.portal.slot.output.tip: What the elves send back lands here
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal0: The elves have learned to fold a whole $(thing)Alfheim gateway$() into a single block: the $(item)Elven Portal$().$(br2)Put in it whatever the elves take, and they send back their trade by the very recipes of the great gateway: $(item)livingwood$() for $(item)dreamwood$(), $(item)manasteel$() for $(item)elementium$(), $(item)mana diamonds$() for $(item)dragonstone$(), and the rest.
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal1: Every trade costs $(thing)500 mana$(), as at the great gateway. The portal holds 100 000 mana and drinks it from the $(item)mana pools$() beside it and from $(item)mana spreaders$() aimed at it.$(br2)While it has mana for a trade, the portal swirls open inside its ring, the runes light up and the natura crystals rise to float over its pedestal.
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal2: Items go in by hand, by $(thing)hoppers and pipes$(), or thrown onto the portal. The nine slots on the left are for the elves, the nine on the right for what they send back: take it out by hand, or with a hopper beneath.$(br2)What the elves only hand back (iron, diamonds, ender pearls) the portal doesn't take at all.
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal3: A pocket gateway, woven from the elves' own gifts.
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal4: The elves refine $(thing)ores$() too: for every block of ore they send back its riches, about as much as a $(item)Fortune II$() pickaxe would find.
alfheimheart.lexicon.portal5: Gems and dusts come back the same way: diamonds, emeralds, lapis, redstone, coal and quartz.
jei.alfheimheart.info.portal: A whole Alfheim gateway in one block. Put items in (by hand, hoppers or pipes, or throw them on it) and the elves trade them by every elven trade recipe, Botania's own and any a pack adds; they also refine ores. Every trade costs 500 mana, which the portal takes from the mana pools beside it and from mana spreaders aimed at it.

gui.alfheimheart.rune_altar.slot.reagent: One block finishes each craft, as on Botania's altar

Manasteel, a mana diamond, a mana pearl: whatever the plate's recipes take
block.alfheimheart.mana_infuser.tip: Infuses items with mana as a mana pool does: manasteel, mana diamonds and pearls, glass, string...
gui.alfheimheart.mana_infuser.hint: Put in what a mana pool infuses: iron, diamonds, ender pearls, glass, string...
gui.alfheimheart.mana_infuser.slot.input: Up to 8 of a kind are infused at once
gui.alfheimheart.mana_infuser.slot.catal: An Alchemy or Conjuration Catalyst: the recipes of a pool standing on it
jei.alfheimheart.info.rune_altar: Botania's Runic Altar in one block. Put the ingredients into its left slots and livingrock into the slot under the altar: it makes the recipe with the most ingredients they fill, by every Runic Altar recipe, using one livingrock a craft. Runes among the ingredients aren't used up. It takes mana from the mana pools beside it and from mana spreaders aimed at it.
jei.alfheimheart.info.terra_plate: Botania's Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate in one block, with no lapis and livingrock round it and no sparks: put in a manasteel ingot, a mana diamond and a mana pearl and it makes terrasteel for 500 000 mana. It holds a million mana, drawn from the mana pools beside it and from mana spreaders aimed at it.
jei.alfheimheart.info.mana_infuser: A mana pool's crafting in one block: whatever a mana pool would infuse, it infuses, up to 8 of a kind at once. An Alchemy or Conjuration Catalyst in its catalyst slot works as the block under a pool does. It takes mana from the mana pools beside it and from mana spreaders aimed at it.
alfheimheart.lexicon.machines0: The elves taught their $(thing)machines$() to do Botania's crafting on their own: an $(item)Elven Runic Altar$(), an $(item)Elven Terrestrial Plate$() and a $(item)Mana Infuser$().$(br2)Each holds its ingredients in nine slots on the left of its window and puts what it makes into nine on the right, by the very recipes of Botania's own altar, plate and pool.
alfheimheart.lexicon.machines1: They drink $(thing)mana$() from the $(item)mana pools$() beside them and from $(item)mana spreaders$() aimed at them, and charge each craft with it, a little at a time. Items go in and out by hand, by $(thing)hoppers and pipes$(); a button in each window sets how it heeds $(thing)redstone$(), and a $(item)comparator$() reads how full its store is.
alfheimheart.lexicon.machines2: The $(item)Elven Runic Altar$() takes livingrock in the slot under its altar, one block a craft. The runes among the ingredients are not used up.
alfheimheart.lexicon.machines3: The $(item)Elven Terrestrial Plate$() needs no lapis, no livingrock round it and no sparks: half a million mana makes an ingot of terrasteel.
alfheimheart.lexicon.machines4: The $(item)Mana Infuser$() infuses up to eight of a kind at once. An $(item)Alchemy$() or $(item)Conjuration Catalyst$() in its catalyst slot works as one under a pool does.
